Roles
MediumRole guide

Mid Lane

The center of the map: big damage, short lane, and the freedom to roam anywhere.

You'll enjoy this role if…

  • You like flashy plays and big bursts of damage.
  • You enjoy aiming skill shots and outplaying your opponent.
  • You want to influence both sides of the map.
  • You like being one of your team's main damage sources.

What this role does

Mid lane is the short lane through the middle of the map. Mid laners are usually mages or assassins who deal big damage, win the lane with clever trades, and roam to help the jungle and the side lanes.

  • Farm and trade well in a short, dangerous lane.
  • Push your wave so you can move first to the river, dragon or side lanes.
  • Roam to help your jungler and other lanes when it's safe.
  • Deal a big share of your team's damage in fights.
  • Watch both rivers and ward them: you're in the middle of everything.

Champion types

  • Control mages like Orianna, Syndra and Malzahar control the fight with crowd control and area damage.
  • Burst mages like Annie, Veigar and Lux can delete a target with one combo.
  • Poke mages like Ziggs damage enemies from very long range and destroy turrets fast.
  • Mobile mages and assassins like Ahri, Aurora and Zed dash in, kill a squishy target and escape.
  • Melee skirmishers like Yasuo use crit and mobility to fight up close. They're harder to play.

We have full guides for every mid laner named here: see the list at the bottom of this page.

Early game (levels 1-6)

Mid lane is short, so your tower is close and you're relatively safe. But ganks can come from both sides, and the enemy jungler reaches you quickly.

  • Start: most mages start Doran's Ring and two Health Potions.
  • Push for priority. Use your abilities to clear the wave faster than your opponent. The laner who pushes first can move to the river first, which wins skirmishes around the Scuttler and dragon.
  • Trade with abilities. Hit your opponent when their key ability is on cooldown or when they walk up to last-hit. See Trading in Lane.
  • Ward both sides. One ward in each side brush or river entrance keeps you safe from ganks.
  • Level 6 is a huge spike for most mid laners. Many can kill an opponent from about half health once they have their ultimate.
Pro tipWhen your opponent disappears from lane, ping them as missing right away, and warn the lane closest to where they went. Mid laners roaming unseen get many kills in low ranks.

Your role quest

The mid lane quest needs 1350 points from farming, plates, takedowns, objectives and time spent in your lane. When you complete it you get:

  • +8% bonus AD and AP, so your damage gets a permanent boost.
  • Free Tier 3 boots: your Tier 2 boots (like Sorcerer's Shoes) upgrade for free to an exclusive Tier 3 version.

You keep earning passive points while you're anywhere in your lane, and after level 3 you can roam for up to 60 seconds without losing progress. That makes short, well-timed roams cheap.

Common mistakeRoaming before level 3 is usually a mistake: you get 25% less minion gold and experience outside your lane until then, and your opponent gets free farm.

Roaming

Roaming is what makes mid lane special. You're the closest laner to every other lane.

Good roams:

  • Push your wave into the enemy tower first, so you don't lose minions while you're away.
  • Go when a side lane has a good setup: an enemy pushed up, low on health, or without Flash.
  • Join your jungler at the Scuttler, Void Grubs or dragon.

Bad roams: leaving with your wave pushed toward you (you'll lose the whole wave and maybe a turret plate), or walking into a lane where the enemy can see you coming.

If your opponent roams, either follow them (ping your teammates) or punish them by pushing their tower and taking plates. Read Roaming and Map Pressure for more.

Mid and late game

After laning, mid laners usually group with the team near dragon or Baron, or catch side waves that come into mid. Keep farming: as a mage, items are your power.

In teamfights:

  • Control mages stay behind the frontline and hit as many enemies as possible.
  • Burst mages and assassins wait for the right moment, then delete the enemy carry.
  • Poke mages chip away at the enemy before the fight starts.

Don't facecheck brushes in the late game. You're squishy, and one catch can lose a Baron. Let a tank or a ward check first. See Teamfighting Basics.

Advanced tips

  • Manage your mana. Spamming abilities on minions leaves you with nothing when the enemy jungler arrives.
  • Track cooldowns. If the enemy mid used their escape, you have a window to all-in. See Matchups, Cooldowns & Lane Priority.
  • Time your recalls with objective spawns, so you're back with full health and new items when dragon appears. See Recall Timing and Tempo.
  • Play around your jungler. Push your wave when your jungler is near, so you can join any fight in the river.
  • Look at the side lanes. After 14 minutes, waves come faster. A mid laner who catches side waves gets a lot of gold.

Beginner-friendly champions

AnnieSimple point-and-click combo and a big stun. Great for learning the lane.
LuxLong range and a safe playstyle. Teaches skill shots and positioning.
VeigarGrows stronger every game with his passive. His cage stuns whole teams.
MalzaharPushes waves easily and his ultimate locks down any target.
AhriMobile and safe with three dashes, and her charm sets up easy kills.

Common mistakes

  • Not warding and dying to the same jungler gank twice.
  • Roaming while your wave is pushing toward your tower and losing tons of farm.
  • Using all your mana on minions and having nothing to fight with.
  • Not pinging when your lane opponent goes missing.
  • Walking into unwarded brush alone in the late game.
